subject: Urgent: Argon Systems - sharp p95/p99 spike after model swap
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@argon-systems.com>

Subject: Sudden latency and 502s after this morning's model swap

Marissa,

We're seeing a major regression since the new model variant was rolled at ~06:00 PT. p95 and p99 latency for our /v1/generate endpoint jumped from ~230ms to 1.6s and we're also seeing intermittent 502s and client timeouts during peak windows. Throughput has dropped as obvious backpressure kicks in. Our product is in the middle of a user-visible release and this is causing timeouts for live users.

Attached: perf_report_v2.3.pdf and a couple of traces I pulled (trace-2028-05-09.log). Please escalate — we need either a fast mitigation or rollback.

Sanjay

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Sudden latency and 502s after this morning's model swap

Marissa / Karthik — initial triage: we've reproduced the p95/p99 uplift locally against v2.3 when replaying Argon traffic. Early signs point to two correlated issues introduced by the variant: 1) tokenization delta increased average sequence lengths for a subset of payloads, driving more attention work per request; 2) a change in kv-cache key layout interacting poorly with our continuous-batching heuristic, resulting in higher cache miss rate and fewer effective batching opportunities.

Observed effects: higher per-token compute and lower batching efficiency => net latency impact and increased request queuing. 502s line up with worker OOM/restart bursts under heavier loads. We're preparing a short perf diff and a suggested rollback plan.

Temporary mitigations we can enact now: reduce canary traffic percentage to 0% for Argon; apply a conservative batching cap to limit per-request memory; and optionally serve a pinned v2.2 for their traffic. I'll post the perf diff and a rollback checklist in the Drive link.

Ben
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Sanjay — update and immediate plan:
- We've reduced Argon's canary traffic to 0% and started an automatic rollback for your tenant to v2.2. That should be effective within the next 10–15 minutes.
- Ben is applying a temporary batching cap across the serving pool to limit memory pressure while we stabilize.
- We're provisioning additional workers in the region to absorb surge while rollback completes.

We know this is disruptive — we'll apply a goodwill credit while we investigate the root cause and verify end-to-end fixes. I'll confirm when traffic is back to normal and share a timeline for RCA.

Can you confirm whether there are any active experiments on your side that might have changed payload distributions recently (e.g., longer prompts, structured JSON fields)? That would help us narrow the tokenization delta.

Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-05-11T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency and 502s after this morning's model swap

Team / Argon — short exec summary and next steps:
- What happened: v2.3 introduced subtle tokenization differences (affecting ~4% of Argon's payloads) that increased average token length and triggered more cache misses in the serving layer. Combined with a change in our KV key derivation for the new variant, this lowered batching efficiency and raised per-request memory pressure. This manifested as p95/p99 spikes and occasional worker restarts => 502s.
- Immediate fix already applied: canary drained; Argon pinned back to v2.2; batching cap and extra workers mitigated crash window.
- Mid-term fixes: revert the KV key layout change for models with legacy tokenizers; add a conservative canary throttling guard that will auto-rollback if queuing or OOM thresholds are exceeded; extend canary observability to include token-length histograms and cache hit-rate metrics.
- Timeline: hotfix for KV layout rollback targeted EOD 2028-05-12; the canary-safety guard targeted by 2028-05-19.

I'll produce the full RCA doc and attach the trace-level diffs. We've also attached the rollback_checklist.xlsx and a draft credit calculation for Argon's downtime.

Karthik
VP, Serving & Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
